title: Monetary Policy and Economic Developments - Federal Reserve
summary: This source is an excerpt from the Federal Reserve's 2018 Annual Report Monetary Policy Report (February 2019), covering monetary policy and economic developments in the second half of 2018. The FOMC raised the target range for the federal funds rate twice in H2 2018 to 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent, then signaled patience at its January 2019 meeting amid softer global conditions and muted inflation. The labor market strengthened with payrolls averaging 224,000/month and unemployment near 4 percent, while PCE inflation fell to 1.7 percent.
key_points: FOMC raised the federal funds rate target range twice in H2 2018, reaching 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent following the December meeting
At the January 2019 meeting, the FOMC indicated it will be patient in determining future adjustments to support maximum employment and price stability
Payroll employment growth averaged 224,000 per month since June 2018
Unemployment rate averaged a little under 4 percent while labor force participation rose
PCE inflation declined from slightly above 2% to an estimated 1.7% in December 2018, restrained by falling energy prices
Core PCE inflation was estimated at 1.9% in December 2018, up 0.25 percentage points from a year prior
Real GDP increased at a solid rate in H2 2018 and rose a little under 3 percent for the year as a whole
Financial conditions tightened late in 2018 amid concerns about global growth outlook and rising US-China trade tensions
Foreign economic growth slowed markedly, especially in the euro area and China
why_it_matters: This Federal Reserve policy record documents the final tightening phase of the 2015-2018 hiking cycle and the transition to a patient stance. The rate level of 2.25-2.50% and the January 2019 'patience' signal foreshadowed the 2019 rate cuts. For market structure analysis, this shows how the FOMC communicated policy shifts during a period of shifting risk sentiment.
macro_context: The report documents a pivot in Fed policy from continued tightening in late 2018 to a patient, wait-and-see posture in early 2019. This occurred amid slowing global growth, muted inflation pressures, and heightened trade tensions. The policy shift preceded the easing actions taken later in 2019.
important_numbers: 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent (federal funds rate target range after December 2018)
224,000 per month (average payroll employment growth since June 2018)
